+---
+#minimax-m3
+
+## What
+Wire MiniMax M3 into the tool-calling and reasoning plumbing in `Libraries/MLXLMCommon`.
+
+- Determine the M3 tool-call emission format from primary sources: the chat template in the mlx-community/MiniMax-M3-4bit checkpoint (`tokenizer_config.json` / `chat_template.jinja`) and upstream mlx-lm PR #1416 (M3 tool-call parsing). Compare against the existing `Libraries/MLXLMCommon/Tool/Parsers/MiniMaxM2ToolCallParser.swift`.
+- If the format matches M2: register the existing parser for the `minimax_m3` / `minimax_m3_vl` model types wherever parser selection is keyed (see `ToolCallFormat.swift`). If it differs: add `MiniMaxM3ToolCallParser.swift` following the M2 parser + `ParserUtilities.swift` conventions.
+- Reasoning/thinking tags: M3 is a thinking model — confirm its tag scheme from the chat template and extend `Libraries/MLXLMCommon/ReasoningConfig.swift` (which already handles MiniMax M2) to cover the M3 model types.
+- Keep behavior for M2 unchanged.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] A captured M3-format tool-call output string (taken verbatim from the checkpoint's chat template examples or upstream PR #1416 fixtures) parses into the expected tool name + arguments
+- [ ] Streaming/partial parse behavior matches the M2 parser's contract (no regressions in `ToolTests`)
+- [ ] Reasoning tags for M3 model types are stripped/segmented per `ReasoningConfig` semantics
+- [ ] M2 parsing and reasoning tests still pass unchanged
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] Extend `Tests/MLXLMTests/ToolTests.swift` and `Tests/MLXLMTests/ReasoningConfigTests.swift` with M3 cases (fixture strings documented with their source)
+- [ ] Run `swift test --filter 'ToolTests|ReasoningConfig'`; expect pass
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass.
\ No newline at end of file
